pages.text: "Grilled shellfish! Yum!" Dari hurried from the mudflats to the kitchen table. With muddy flippers, he grabbed a warm shell. "Your flippers?" Mom asked. Dari pretended not to hear and ate.
"Washing takes too long! I'll eat and play again!" His cheeks bulged. Tiny smiling wrigglers hopped from his muddy flippers onto the shellfish.
Soon Dari's tummy rumbled and ached. "Oh, my tummy..." He rubbed it, eyes watering. Kongal watched from the cradle.

Mom examined his flippers. "Mud wrigglers rode the shellfish into your tummy." She put freshly washed Kongal's flipper beside Dari's. One shiny, one black and gritty. Dari lowered his nose toward his own.
They stood by the wooden bathroom tub. "Three steps! One, get them wet!" Mom poured water with a dipper. The wrigglers on Dari's flippers shrank back.
"Two, make soapy bubbles!" Dari rubbed both flippers. White foam rose. "Like wave foam!" Mom sang, "Wash until you're squeaky clean, then eat!"
"Three, scrub and rinse every corner, between your flippers, too!" Dari rubbed and rinsed the wrigglers away. "One, two, three—squeaky clean! Bye, wrigglers!"
Patting dry left soft, shiny flippers. His tummy gradually felt better. Dari held a flipper beside Kongal's; both gleamed. He slapped his tail. "Washing first will keep my tummy happy!"
That evening, Dari called first. "Wait! Flippers before food! One, wet! Two, bubbles! Three, squeaky clean!" Now he could do it alone.
Mom touched her nose to Dari's. "Our washing champion!" Washing before eating kept his tummy happy and left him fresh. Wash until you're squeaky clean! Today's shellfish tasted twice as good.
